newsitem.title: FINLAND: Tamro repeats sees 97 profit steady on 96.
newsitem.headline: Tamro repeats sees 97 profit steady on 96.

text.p: Finnish pharmaceuticals wholesaler Oy Tamro Ab repeated on Tuesday that it saw no major changes in 1997 profits compared to 1996, but that profitability would depend partly on the Swedish crown's exchange rate.

"The 1997 net sales and result after financial items are forecast to remain virtually at the previous year's levels, provided that the Swedish crown stays at the level (where) it was at the beginning of the year," Tamro said in a statement with its 19996 results.
In 1996, Tamro's prfit after financial items rose to 224 million markka from 155 million. @
"The competitive situation in the distribution sector of the group's market area has clearly stiffened while the growth of other health-care products has leveled out," Tamro said.
The profit trend for the Pharma distribution division in Finland, the Baltic states and northwest Russia was expected to remain favorable, Tamro said.

"In Norway, a clearly improved financial result is anticipated. The profit level in Sweden is, however, likely to decline owing to the sharp uptrend in the year-end (1996) demand for pharmaceuticals and the subsequently stagnant sales in 1997," Tamro said. @
Cost-efficiency in Sweden would be improved and the workforce there cut by about 10 percent in 1997, it added.

Group activities in 1997 would focus on further developing the Nordic distribution concept and joint data management systems, on securing profits from corporate acquisitions and improving the performance at Pharma Distribution Norway.
The possibilities of further expanding the operations of the medical and laboratory division and extending distribution services to Denmark were being charted, it said.
Only the Tamda unit, active in the Baltic republics, remained slightly in the red, Tamro said, referring to 1996. @
"But even this drawback is likely to be remedied by the end of 1997," it said.

Tamro's board has set a long-term goal of achieving a 15 percent annual increase in earnings per share, and a target for return on equity to exceed the yield of Finnish long-term bonds by five percentage points, the company said.
In 1996, Tamro's EPS rose 38.7 percent to 1.73 markka. The group's ROE was 9.5 percent compared to 7.9 percent in 1995.

On Tuesday afternoon, the yield on Finnish government benchmark bonds maturing in 2001 was around 4.60 percent and the yield on bonds maturing in 2006 was just below 5.90 percent. @ --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
